main_text.l: pta ferunt: ac sibi videantur esse felicissimi. Sunt qui se solos verae religionis asserto-res esse opinentur, quum tamen tetra opi-nionum monstra propugnent: traditi in iu-dicij expertem mentem: ac conseruos suos inhumaniter caedant.

Rursum sunt qui iugum ab adolescentia sua portant, qui haeresio infimulantur, qui ob veritatis professionem inhumanissime proscribuntur: qui deniq; cum Dauide dicant: Sepe afflixerunt me a iuuentute mea; nec tamen potuerunt quicquam contra me. Supra dorsum meum araverunt aratores & produxerunt sulcos suos. Iehouah est iustus, concidit fines impiorum. Psal 129 v.2.3.4.
His mundus quidem prae illis calamitosas esse opinatur. Spiritus vero sanctus, hoc quidem in medijs aerumnis foelices: illos vero in media prosperitate infoelices, vere pronunciat.

Huius ergo iudicio ipsi quoq; stemus & sepenumero repetamus ista verba: Pro summo gaudio ducite, fratres mei, quoties in tentationes varias incideritis: illud scien-tes probationem fidei vestrae, parere patien-tiam. Iac.1.2.3.
Da nobis Domine Iesu, ut calicem, quem Pater tuus coelestis nobis propinat, vt nos erui-

page.notes: Page is a continuation page of the Obadiah commentary. The final line is cut off at the foot ("erui-" continues on the next page). Several words are hard to read in the scan, notably "calamitosas" (printed as "calamito/fas"), "sepenumero" and "iugum", which I have transcribed as best read. Parts of the Psalm and Epistle references are faint; the reference "Pfal 129 v.1.2.3.4." is read as printed. Show-through and stains are ignored. Two words near "Pro summo" are slightly smudged but legible. The printed text uses long s and the "vt" spelling; I have kept the printed forms, changing only u/v and i/j where needed.
